namespacing.compared_how: Per drug, the QED component against the drugs.json descriptor rounded as drugs.json stores it, so storage rounding is not mistaken for a difference of definition. max_abs_diff is the raw difference and can be a rounding step (5e-4) even where n_different is 0.
namespacing.note: Two descriptor families, never to be mixed. 'qed.*' are the eight properties QED itself scores, as rdkit.Chem.QED.properties() defines them. 'd.*' are the descriptors site/data/drugs.json already stores, as tools/build_data.py computed them (Crippen.MolLogP, Crippen.MolMR, CalcTPSA, Descriptors.MolWt, CalcNumLipinskiHBD / CalcNumLipinskiHBA, CalcNumRotatableBonds default, CalcNumAromaticRings, CalcFractionCSP3, PubChem complexity, rule-of-five violations). Same name, different definition: QED's HBA counts matches of its own acceptor SMARTS, its HBD is CalcNumHBD, its ROTB is the Strict definition and its AROM counts the rings left after the aliphatic rings are deleted. Each summary key carries its own 'source'.

per_drug_keys.alerts: indices into meta.alerts.list of the alert SMARTS that match this drug; len(alerts) == qed_props.ALERTS

stats.hist: fixed bins, count by Freedman-Diaconis h = 2 IQR n^(-1/3), clipped at 60 bins; integer-valued properties spanning at most 60 get one bin per value, edges on the half-integers
stats.kde: gaussian kernel, Silverman bandwidth, 64 samples over the observed range; y is normalised to a peak of 1, peak_density carries the scale
stats.quantiles: statistics.quantiles(n=4, method='inclusive'); p1 and p99 from n=100, present when n is at least 20, there so a page can clip an axis away from the long peptide tail
stats.rounding: 4 dp for summary statistics and the normalised curve, 3 dp for per-drug float properties, 6 significant digits for bandwidths and densities
